patch_description:
The previous program was fundamentally broken: it added an "original_index" column to the data, returned empty column_orderings (invalid per-row orderings), used fragile Counter-based value arithmetic that fails on mixed-type/unhashable cells, built result frames via `result_df.loc[i]` on empty DataFrames (never populating rows correctly), and its assertions on shapes failed (e.g., final shape mismatch when discarding columns). None of its machinery actually targeted the real objective (serial character-Trie reuse).

The fix replaces the whole editable block with a correct, bounded algorithm:
- Serialize each cell exactly as the evaluator does ("" for missing, str otherwise) for scoring only, preserving stored values.
- Build up to three cheap candidate constructions: (1) global column order ranked by sum(len(v)*count*(count-1)), (2) a rank ignoring length, (3) a conditional partition tree over integer factorization codes choosing split columns by length-weighted pair repetition, with bounded depth/candidates and a deterministic global-rank tail.
- Score each candidate with the exact ideal Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs of sorted serialized rows, computed with C-speed binary-search prefix comparisons, identical strings handled directly).
- Return the best candidate as a per-row permuted DataFrame (object dtype) with valid per-row column orderings; all rows/values preserved. col_merge is honored via the parent's merging_columns when available, and API parameters (early_stop, row_stop, col_stop, distinct_value_threshold, parallel) are accepted and used as bounds only.
